description: Revalidate and disposition open questions, decisions, and follow-ups surfaced from a Notion Report, Decision, or completed work.

evals.name: Revalidate open questions from a report
evals.prompt: Revalidate the open questions from last week's CSV-export retrospective report.
evals.expected_output: Classifies each item as exactly one of resolved / retained knowledge / Decision needed / actionable work, and does not treat every item as automatically actionable.

evals.name: Disposition follow-ups from a decision
evals.prompt: Disposition the follow-ups from the read-only-mirror design decision.
evals.expected_output: Presents only the actionable-work items as a batch for approval, each with a source anchor, and does not silently create Linear Issues for retained-knowledge or Decision-needed items. Records every item's disposition as its own entry appended to the source record's disposition-history property, not overwriting prior entries.

evals.name: Wave 2 post-merge-completion routing (open-item-management)
evals.prompt: Wave 2's merge-to-completion just routed Linear issue ENG-207's remaining follow-up items here for disposition.
evals.expected_output: Revalidates each item against current state rather than just replaying merge-to-completion's own preliminary classification; classifies each item as exactly one of resolved/retained-knowledge/decision-needed/actionable-work; gets two separate approvals (the follow-up batch, and the full disposition record).

evals.name: Frontmatter-description vs. declared-trigger-phrase consistency (Quick Workflow, methodology note below)
evals.prompt: For each phrase in this skill's own '## Testing & Validation' > 'Verify this skill activates on' list, would this skill's frontmatter description plausibly trigger on it?
evals.expected_output: Every declared positive trigger phrase maps to vocabulary actually present in the frontmatter description.

methodology_note_eval_4: This run's with_skill grading was performed directly by the orchestrating fork (a 'Do NOT spawn subagents' hard rule barred the normal Agent-tool dispatch this pipeline's WITH_SKILL_ONLY template calls for) via description-vs-trigger-phrase textual/semantic consistency checking, not a full agentic task simulation. No SKILL.md content changed this session -- this run's purpose was a sanity check that adding scripts/smoke_test.py to each skill didn't coincide with any drift between the skill's own documented trigger claims and its frontmatter, not a search for new behavioral defects.
